thread.title: Apple Display Development News Hits Universal Display Shares

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Display Development News Hits Universal Display Shares
text:
A report that Apple ( AAPL ) is developing its own device displays using next-generation MicroLED screens took down shares of Universal Display ( OLED ), a provider of an alternative display technology.
X Bloomberg reported Sunday that Apple has made a significant investment in MicroLED or light-emitting diode displays. The screens use different compounds than the organic light-emitting diode, or OLED displays that Universal provides. The MicroLED screens, though, offer similar advantages — such as slimmer screens and lower power consumption than liquid-crystal display, or LCD screens. Apple is designing and producing MicroLED displays in test quantities at a secret manufacturing plant near its headquarters in Cupertino, Calif., Bloomberg said.
MicroLED displays are much more difficult to produce than OLED displays and it could be a few years before they are used in Apple products, like the Apple Watch and iPhone, Bloomberg said.
Universal Display shares plunged 12.1% to close at 109 . The Ewing, N.J.-based company is a key supplier of technology and materials used to make OLED displays. Its stock has come under pressure in recent weeks amid reports that Apple has cut production of the iPhone X, its first OLED-screen smartphone. Apple gets its OLED screens from Samsung, a Universal Display customer.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Universal Display stock hit an all-time high of 209 on Jan. 19, before heading south. Apple also uses OLED screens in its current Apple Watch smartwatches. It sources those screens from Sharp, another Universal Display customer.
News that Apple is developing MicroLED displays also impacted shares of major display makers. LG Display ( LPL ) stock lost 1.9% to 12.82.
Also Monday, brokerage firm Nomura Instinet lowered its iPhone sales forecast for 2018 after its checks showed little improvement in iPhone demand recently.
"Corresponding supply chain downticks suggest iPhone expectations have yet to bottom," Instinet analyst Jeffrey Kvaal said in a report. "Our Taiwan team reduced iPhone X estimates last night."
Instinet cut its total iPhone sales estimate for Apple's fiscal 2018 to 221 million units from 226 million. It's now below consensus estimates of 224 million, Kvaal said. Apple's fiscal 2018 runs through Sept. 29.
He reiterated his neutral rating on Apple stock with a price target of 175.
Apple shares slipped 1.5% to finish at 175.30.
